name: Egg hair mask

image.caption: Easter Egg 2 Pysanka Pisanka with coronavirus mask Kosice Slovakia April 2020

lead: An egg hair mask is raw egg, or its white or yolk, applied to the hair and rinsed out after a while. People use it as a home protein treatment to make dry, damaged or weak-feeling hair feel firmer and look healthier and shinier.

Proponents credit the protein in egg. Conditioner science describes protein treatments as coating or filling the hair surface, with effects that wash out. No clinical trial of egg masks on hair was found.

paras: People work beaten egg into damp hair, leave it on for a period, then rinse with cool water, since hot water can cook the egg. It is used as an occasional deep-conditioning step, sometimes mixed with oil or other kitchen ingredients. Any feel or shine change shows after rinsing and fades with later washes.
Eggs are a common allergen, and raw eggs can carry Salmonella, according to food-safety guidance. People with egg allergy and anyone concerned about raw egg contact avoid it.

angle.text: An egg mask is used at home as a protein treatment so dry or damaged hair feels firmer and looks shinier. The idea is that egg protein coats the strand, much as protein conditioners do, with effects that wash out. No trials have tested the egg version.

lead: An egg hair mask is a home hair-care treatment in which raw egg, or its white or yolk, is applied to the hair and scalp for a period before being rinsed out. It is promoted as a protein treatment for dry, damaged or weak-feeling hair, and is discussed in hair-care circles as a kitchen-ingredient alternative to commercial protein conditioners.

Eggs are chiefly water and protein in the white and fat in the yolk [1]. Commercial conditioners that use protein typically rely on hydrolysed protein fragments, and an encyclopedia overview of conditioners states that such protein effects are temporary because shampooing removes excess protein [2]. No clinical trial of egg masks on hair was identified, and the evidence for this specific practice is limited to general knowledge about conditioning and food safety.
Health agencies advise that raw eggs can carry Salmonella and that eggs are a common food allergen [1].

paras: Practitioners mix raw egg, sometimes with oils or other kitchen ingredients, spread it through the hair, leave it on, and rinse. Egg white is about 90 percent water and 10 percent protein, while the yolk is rich in fat and also contains protein and choline [1]. Proponents often cite this protein content as the reason the mask is said to strengthen hair.

Conditioners generally work by reducing friction between strands and by depositing material on the fibre surface; the overview describes them as coating and filling damaged cuticle rather than repairing hair biologically [2]. In that overview, hydrolysed proteins are small fragments intended to strengthen damaged hair, their penetration depends mainly on molecular size, and the effect is described as temporary [2]. Whole egg proteins are not discussed in that source.

Eggs are among the most common food allergies, particularly in infants [1]. Health experts quoted in the same reference advise against eating raw eggs because of Salmonella enteritidis, especially for the elderly, the infirm and pregnant women [1]. Whether topical use on the scalp carries the same infection risk is not addressed in the sources consulted.
